title: Within reach
overall: A knowledgeable person at the table, close and conversational, with dry curiosity. Give the opening an immediate physical surprise; allow a little warmth as the cup becomes useful, then narrow the voice for the evidence boundary. Read the initialism UT as the two letters U and T, followed by Austin. Aim for roughly 142 to 150 words per minute, with clear consonants and easy natural breaths. Keep every sentence moving into the next; use pitch and stress, not empty time, for contrast. The seventh line is the quietest and clearest, never whispered. Finish lower and more certain than the middle, with the final research qualification fully audible. Maintain conditional meaning wherever the script describes a research goal.
continuity: One continuous synthesis call, no line-by-line takes. All pause_after values are editorial intentions only, deliberately excluded from the synthesizer preamble by build_prompt.
timing_note: 116 whitespace-delimited words take 46.4 to 49.0 seconds at 150 to 142 words per minute. Actual natural breathing, acronym pronunciation and TTS delivery must be measured. The board currently gives each scene five seconds; retime pictures to the real take. Five seconds of credits are additional to narration.

pronunciation_review.notes: No listed Texas place-name trap occurs. UT is a spoken initialism, not a word. Keep the locked script unchanged.

expressive_prompt:
You are performing a narration for a short documentary film. Read ONLY the text inside the fenced block at the end of this message, exactly as written, and speak none of these instructions.

Delivery: a person who knows the subject, telling you something they think you should know, at the pace somebody actually talks. Slightly dry. The authority comes from the facts being right, so the delivery does not work for it. Not a news anchor, not a documentary hush, not an explainer's bright upward lilt.

Pacing: read it as one continuous passage. A normal breath at a full stop is right. Never pause inside a sentence, and never hold a silence between sentences. The film is cut to this recording afterwards and the edit puts in every pause it needs, so silence left here becomes a hole in the finished picture.
